To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The heat transfer coefficient between shell-side fluid (liquid nitrogen) and shell wall in spiral wound heat exchanger is a function of Reynolds number and geometrical parameters of the heat exchanger; (2) A new correlation for Nusselt number in the spiral wound heat exchanges is developed and validated using CFD simulations.
the Nusselt number correlation is proposed for the shell side of SWHEs in terms of Reynolds and geometrical parameters.

the Nusselt number correlation in terms of the Reynolds number, non-dimensional shell-side diameter, and non-dimensional baffle spacing is proposed to predict the heat transfer between the SWHE shell wall and the shell-side fluid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical simulation of the heat transfer between the heat exchangers shell-side fluid and wall.
the heat transfer characteristics between shell-side fluid flow and shell wall of SWHEs, which is essential to the design and optimization of SWHEs.
the development of a new correlation to predict the heat transfer coefficient in SWHEs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heat-in-leaks between the shell-side fluids and shell wall can be predicted using the developed correlations.
the heat transfer coefficient between the shell-side flow and the shell wall in the SWHEs can be estimated by using the Nusselt number correlation proposed in this study.
the Nusselt number in the spiral-wind heat exchangers can be accurately predicted by the proposed correlations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Nusselt number correlation for SWHEs is developed and the thermal entrance length for SWHEs has been specified.
the developed correlations could be used for predicting the heat transfer between the SWHE shell-side fluid and its wall.
the developed correlations can be applied in heat-in-leak calculation in the SWHEs with the average error of 6.1%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Nusselt number in the entrance and the fully developed regions can be correlated with the geometrical and fluid parameters.
the thermal entrance length is an important parameter to be taken into account in the heat-inleak calculations.
the developed Nusselt number model can be used for heat-in-leak analysis in SWHEs.
